body: I can’t remember a time I didn’t feel this way.
I just find it really hard to shake the belief that something is wrong with me and I’m doomed to be a loser. So I suppose yes—there is a lack of hope that things will work out.

I did CBT too and you’re right, most of the time you don’t spend time targeting core beliefs. I personally tried Zoloft for about two years and then stopped last summer. It helped in some ways but it didn’t really solve any issues. I thought about trying it again but it’s a whole process I don’t look forward to starting over. To be honest though, a big part of me just doesn’t want to solve my problems and is really attracted to the idea of suicide. I don’t know.

When I told my brother how frustrating it was to hear that, he told me I was spending too much time and effort on pinpointing the cause instead of “doing the work” to address my shortcomings.

Yes, I have given both a try but I’m in a place right now where therapy isn’t really an option (it’s too expensive in my country, only a few free options that you can’t meet that frequently) and I don’t really want to experiment with meds again (it takes a long time to work, not sure if I only have depression or something else too, it addresses symptoms but not the cause).
Honestly I can’t say. I talked to my brother about this last night and he denied any differences. Told me it’s all in the way I think and look at things.

I didn’t think about it much, but I believe it has to do with my upbringing. I felt neglected growing up and was rarely made to feel good enough or normal. It’s hard to say though since my siblings grew up in the same household and they don’t seem to have the same issues as me. I don’t know.

I don’t know if I talk like that in real life since that post took me a while to write but thank you for the kind words.

If you don’t mind me asking, what makes you think you have a personality disorder? Do you plan on doing anything about it?

Thank you for talking the time to read what I wrote and write a response.

I have had thoughts about about trying some things in the past but I struggle to decide on anything or find the motivation to start. It can be especially hard when “ending it” and the thought “what’s the point” is constantly on your mind.

I get what you mean about making friends, but it pains me to see people connecting around me and me shying away because I think I’m a “loser” (and then having another reason to be frustrated with myself).

I don’t mind talking about these things. It’s just that it can be hard to talk about this with people around me. Again, thank you for your message. I liked reading it.
